sections.content: Savannah, Georgia has quietly become one of the most compelling real estate markets in the Southeast. With a booming tourism economy, a growing port industry, and an influx of remote workers drawn to its historic charm and lower cost of living, investors are finding real estate deals in Savannah GA that are hard to match in larger metros. Whether you're a first-time investor or a seasoned wholesaler, this market deserves a serious look. If you're just getting started, our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide is a great place to build your foundation before diving into a specific market like Savannah.
Savannah GA Real Estate Market Overview

Savannah is the oldest city in Georgia and home to roughly 150,000 residents, with the greater Chatham County area pushing past 300,000. The local economy is anchored by the Port of Savannah, one of the busiest ports on the East Coast, along with major employers like Gulfstream Aerospace, Memorial Health, and a thriving hospitality sector. The Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD) adds a steady stream of students and young professionals to the rental market year-round. Together, these economic drivers create strong, consistent housing demand that investors love.
Average Home Prices in Savannah

As of 2024, the median home price in Savannah sits around $290,000 to $320,000, up significantly from under $200,000 just five years ago. However, prices vary widely by neighborhood. Historic District homes and renovated properties near Forsyth Park can easily exceed $600,000, while distressed properties in emerging neighborhoods on the south and west sides of the city can still be purchased in the $80,000 to $150,000 range. This price spread is exactly what creates opportunity for wholesalers, flippers, and buy-and-hold investors alike. You can explore current deal activity in this market at [AIWholesail's Savannah GA market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/savannah-ga).
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Savannah

Not all of Savannah's zip codes are created equal for investors. Some areas are better suited for short-term rental plays, others for long-term buy-and-hold, and some for wholesale or fix-and-flip strategies. Here are the neighborhoods worth putting on your radar.

items: Midtown Savannah: A transitional neighborhood with solid rental demand and homes priced between $150,000 and $280,000. Strong appreciation potential as gentrification pushes outward from the Historic District.
Starland District: Hip, arts-focused area popular with SCAD students and young renters. Short-term rentals and house hacks work well here. Median prices around $250,000 to $350,000.
Baldwin Park: Emerging neighborhood on the southside with affordable distressed inventory. Great for wholesalers and flippers targeting ARVs of $180,000 to $250,000.
Ardsley Park / Chatham Crescent: Stable, established neighborhood with craftsman bungalows. Lower turnover but strong long-term rental and flip margins.
West Savannah: The highest concentration of distressed and off-market properties. Higher risk but also the highest potential spreads for experienced wholesalers and flippers.
Pooler (Savannah suburbs): Rapidly growing suburb with new construction demand and strong rental occupancy rates near Interstate 95 and the Savannah airport corridor.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Savannah
Wholesale Deals

Savannah has a healthy wholesale market, particularly in West Savannah and parts of Midtown where absentee owners, probate properties, and tax-delinquent homes create motivated seller situations. A typical wholesale deal in Savannah might involve a property with an ARV of $200,000 that needs $40,000 in repairs, acquired under contract for $95,000 and assigned to a cash buyer for a $10,000 to $15,000 assignment fee. To sharpen your skills in this strategy, check out the [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide. To run your own numbers quickly, use the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator).
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

Flipping in Savannah works best in neighborhoods with clear comps and strong buyer demand. Ardsley Park and Midtown both have proven flip markets where renovated homes sell quickly to owner-occupants and vacation home buyers. A well-executed flip in these areas can yield $40,000 to $80,000 in profit on a three- to four-month timeline. The key is buying right. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate your after-repair value before you ever make an offer. Overpaying for a flip in Savannah is easy to do, especially as prices have risen fast — accurate ARV math is non-negotiable.
Rental Properties and Short-Term Rentals

Savannah is one of the top tourist destinations in the United States, drawing over 14 million visitors per year. That foot traffic has made short-term rentals (Airbnb and VRBO) extremely lucrative in and around the Historic District. A well-positioned two-bedroom property near River Street or Forsyth Park can generate $4,000 to $6,000 per month in gross short-term rental income. For long-term landlords, average rents in Savannah run $1,200 to $1,800 per month for single-family homes, with strong occupancy supported by SCAD enrollment, port workers, and military families from nearby Fort Stewart.

Pro Tip: Before investing in short-term rentals in Savannah, check Chatham County's current STR ordinance. The city has implemented permit requirements and zoning restrictions in certain districts. Always verify local regulations before buying — what's allowed today can change with the next city council vote.
Savannah Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

Several macro and local trends are shaping the Savannah market right now. First, inventory remains historically low, which continues to put upward pressure on prices even as mortgage rates have cooled buyer demand. Second, the Port of Savannah continues to expand, with billions in infrastructure investment underway that will bring thousands of jobs to the region over the next decade. Third, remote work migration from the Northeast continues to bring higher-income buyers who are pushing prices up in premium neighborhoods. For investors, this means the window for finding deeply discounted on-market deals is narrow — which is why off-market deal sourcing is more important than ever in this market.

"The investors winning in secondary markets like Savannah aren't finding deals on the MLS — they're building direct-to-seller pipelines before properties ever hit the market." — Common wisdom among experienced real estate wholesalers in the Southeast
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Savannah

Savannah is attracting a growing number of out-of-state investors, particularly from New York, New Jersey, California, and Florida who see strong relative value compared to their home markets. Investing remotely comes with real risks, but with the right team and systems, it's very manageable. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) remotely is one of the most valuable skills you can develop before targeting a new market.

items: Build your local team first: Find a real estate attorney, a local property manager, a reliable general contractor, and a title company before you buy anything. Savannah has a strong investor community, and referrals move fast.

Visit the market at least once: Savannah's neighborhood quality changes block by block, especially in transitional areas. A single market visit will save you from costly mistakes that Zillow photos can't reveal.

Focus on off-market leads: The best deals in Savannah aren't on the MLS. Direct mail to absentee owners, driving for dollars in target zip codes, and building relationships with local wholesalers are the most reliable sourcing strategies.
Understand the landlord-tenant laws: Georgia is generally considered a landlord-friendly state with relatively straightforward eviction procedures, which is a plus for out-of-state rental investors.
Run your numbers conservatively: Factor in property management fees (8-10%), vacancy rates (5-8%), and Savannah's humidity-related maintenance costs, which can be higher than drier climates.

Analyze deals thoroughly: Don't rely on gut feel. Learn [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to make sure every acquisition meets your return criteria before you commit.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating rental properties in Savannah, aim for a gross rent multiplier (GRM) of 10 or lower in emerging neighborhoods, and a cash-on-cash return of at least 8% after all expenses. The market has appreciated significantly, so deals that pencil on cash flow are fewer — but they still exist if you're sourcing off-market.
Is Savannah GA Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Savannah offers something for nearly every type of real estate investor. Wholesalers will find motivated sellers in distressed neighborhoods. Flippers will find strong buyer demand in transitional areas. Rental investors will find dependable long-term tenants and exceptional short-term rental income potential. And appreciation-focused buyers will find a city with strong economic fundamentals that point toward continued price growth. The key is knowing your strategy, understanding the local submarkets, and moving quickly when the right deal appears. Savannah is no longer a secret — but it's also not yet overrun the way Atlanta or Nashville have become.
